text:
amanda_sales: Quick thread — customer (large fintech) asking if we can support a 7-year retention/archival requirement for their customer-managed keys. They want: 1) contract language that keys are retained under customer control, 2) an availability SLA for key unwrap ops during legal holds, and 3) whether we can offer a limited escrow workflow or if we require customer escrow. Any blockers?

dave_sre: tl;dr we can keep keys in their KMS (customer-managed) — Redwood Private/VPC is fine. Availability SLA for unwrap depends on deployment mode. Dedicated/Private can get SLA, hosted less so. :thinking:

nima_eng: For hosted API we proxy calls to customer's KMS (if BYOK) — unwrap latency depends on their KMS. We can add retries and local caching of wrapped tokens for short windows, but multi-year retention doesn't change runtime logic. Important: if customer expects Redwood to hold raw key material that's an immediate no.

clare_legal: Contract notes: we should accept a clause that affirms customer retains key ownership. For escrow: legal will need specifics — are they asking us to escrow plaintext, or a wrapped backup? We must not store plaintext keys. If they want escrow, propose a process where escrow is held by a neutral third party under customer control.

amanda_sales: They explicitly asked if Redwood can be the escrow holder for an enterprise-only deal. Also asked about rotation windows and whether rotation events count as downtime for SLA.

rachel_prod: Rotation: we support live rotation with zero-downtime patterns if the customer uses wrapping + new key publish. If their KMS has maintenance windows, that’s external. For contract SLA, we can state "availability of key unwrap for requests routed to Dedicated/Private is covered by infra SLA; hosted is best-effort with recommended mitigation patterns."

dave_sre: Actionable: 1) decline to hold plaintext or raw KEKs. 2) Offer documented escrow option via third-party custodian (we can recommend partners). 3) For SLA wording — we can include a carveout for customer-controlled KMS downtime. 4) Tech preflight: need customer's KMS endpoints, expected QPS, and rotation cadence.

amanda_sales: ok — customer will push back on third-party escrow; asks for pricing delta if Redwood offers a managed escrow (holding wrapped backup only). Is that something we can quote?

nima_eng: We can offer a managed-wrapped-backup service (store wrapped key blobs, never unwrapped), but ops & compliance must sign off. It’s additional storage + audit + restricted ops; treat as an add-on. Estimate: minimal infra cost but compliance overhead — sales can add a placeholder line item: "managed key backup (wrapped-only) — custom quote."

clare_legal: If we do managed wrapped backup, require documented separation of duties, customer-signed attestation, and limited access roles. Also require indemnity language for escrow retrieval requests.

ops_bot: deploy-bot: reminder — any feature flagged as "managed key backup" needs a SOC/PCI review ticket before quoting. Ticket template: /new-compliance-review <feature> <customer> <scope>.

amanda_sales: Next steps I propose: 1) send customer a short note (I'll draft) saying Redwood cannot hold plaintext keys, can provide wrapped-only managed backup as add-on (subject to review), and that SLA for unwrap is available on Dedicated/Private with carveouts for customer KMS downtime; 2) request KMS endpoints/QPS/rotation cadence; 3) loop in legal for escrow language. Anyone object?

clare_legal: Sounds good. I'll draft suggested contract language snippets they can attach to the SOW.

dave_sre: I'll prep a short ops appendix outlining availability expectations and the caching/timeout behavior we recommend.

nima_eng: I'll list required integration points and a minimal test plan (wrap/unwrap smoke, rotation dry-run).

amanda_sales: Great — I'll schedule a 30m sync with the customer for tomorrow 10am PT. Will post meeting invite and the draft note. :thumbsup:

rachel_prod: FYI add a line that rotation DRY-RUN is required before go-live for managed backup cases.

amanda_sales: noted — thanks all.
